result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.is_isomorphic()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Check if this graph is isomorphic to another graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L6357-L6466){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.is_isomorphic(other) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Is isomorphic](/assets/graphs/is-isomorphic.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Each side compares graph g with graph h. Left: g is a five-node cycle and h is the same cycle redrawn as a star, so is_isomorphic(h) returns True. Right: h is a triangle with a two-edge tail; it has the same node and edge counts, but its degree-3 node C and degree-1 node E (shown in the accent color) have no match in the cycle, so is_isomorphic(h) returns False." width="100%"} Two graphs are isomorphic if there exists a one-to-one correspondence (bijection) between their nodes that preserves the adjacency relationship. In simpler terms, they have the same structure but possibly different node labels. This implementation checks the following necessary conditions: - same number of nodes - same number of edges - same degree sequence - same directedness ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [other]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Another `Graph` object to compare with. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `True` if graphs satisfy isomorphism conditions, `False` otherwise. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} A true isomorphism between graphs $G_1$ and $G_2$ is a bijection $\pi: V_1 \to V_2$ such that $(u, v) \in E_1 \iff (\pi(u), \pi(v)) \in E_2$. Deciding whether such a $\pi$ exists is the graph isomorphism problem, famous for sitting in $\mathsf{NP}$ but not known to be in $\mathsf{P}$ or $\mathsf{NP}\text{-complete}$, and solved in practice by backtracking algorithms like VF2 or Babai's quasi-polynomial procedure. This method instead checks a handful of cheap *invariants* (node count, edge count, degree sequence, directedness) which any isomorphism must preserve. Two graphs that disagree on any invariant are provably non-isomorphic, but agreement is only suggestive: many non-isomorphic graphs share the same degree sequence. Use this as a fast filter before running a full isomorphism check. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Two paths of the same length are isomorphic even though their node labels differ -- what matters is the structure, not the names: ::: {#a71e8383 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g1 = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "C") ) g2 = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_node(label="X") .add_node(label="Y") .add_node(label="Z") .add_edge("X", "Y") .add_edge("Y", "Z") ) g1.is_isomorphic(g2) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` True ``` ::: ::: A path and a star of the same size have different degree sequences, so they're correctly ruled out: ::: {#9f0a93cf .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} path = ec.Graph(directed=False).add_path_graph(n=4) star = ec.Graph(directed=False).add_star_graph(n=4) path.is_isomorphic(star) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` False ``` ::: ::: Directedness is compared too, so an otherwise-identical directed and undirected graph don't count as isomorphic: ::: {#ef5943e7 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} directed = ec.Graph(directed=True).add_path_graph(n=3) undirected = ec.Graph(directed=False).add_path_graph(n=3) directed.is_isomorphic(undirected) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` False ``` ::: ::: Two complete graphs of the same size are always isomorphic, since every node is interchangeable: ::: {#1665653b .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} k4_a = ec.Graph(directed=False).add_full_graph(n=4) k4_b = ec.Graph(directed=False).add_full_graph(n=4) k4_a.is_isomorphic(k4_b) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` True ``` ::: ::: Graphs of different sizes can never be isomorphic: ::: {#17641aea .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} g3 = ec.Graph(directed=False).add_cycle_graph(n=3) g4 = ec.Graph(directed=False).add_cycle_graph(n=4) g3.is_isomorphic(g4) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ``` False ``` ::: :::
